title: Enforce service tenant isolation with claim-aggregator, KMS escrow and immutable audit bridge
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Adds tenant-boundary claim aggregator, KMS escrow path for tenant-scoped keys, and an immutable audit bridge that signs and seals audit envelopes. Default rollout is shadow mode with gradual enforcement; no customer-visible API changes.
commits_summary: introduce tenant claim aggregator service; wire aggregator into auth pipeline; add kms-escrow allocator and tests; implement immutable-audit-bridge and signing agent; add integration tests for residency and fallback; fix race in claim cache; update docs and rollout script
description: Motivation: Some operator and cross-tenant paths were able to surface KMS-wrapped artifacts and audit records without an explicit tenant binding, increasing blast radius during operator escalation. This PR implements a small, composable enforcement surface that performs three coordinated tasks: (1) aggregate and normalize tenant assertions at the edge, (2) allocate a short-lived KMS escrow key tied to the tenant claim for cryptographic operations that require strict locality, and (3) emit audit envelopes through an immutable audit bridge which signs and seals events before delivery to long-term storage. Design summary: The claim-aggregator service collects claims from auth headers, session tokens and upstream directories; it produces a canonical tenant assertion that is cached per-request with a TTL and HMAC fingerprint. The kms-escrow allocator returns a tenant-scoped transient CMK handle (wrapped key material) and records a minimal provenance record. The immutable audit bridge converts internal audit records into a sealed protobuf envelope, signs with the escrowed key and forwards to audit-plane; envelopes include a region and residency tag to aid downstream retention. Operational considerations: default behavior is shadow mode where assertions, KMS allocations and sealed envelopes are emitted to a separate shadow stream; enforcement gates are feature-flagged and can be turned on per-cluster. Rollout plan: 1) deploy aggregator and bridge in shadow mode; 2) enable KMS escrow allocation for sampling traffic; 3) enable enforcement for internal operator flows; 4) full enforcement by tenant cohort. Backout plan: flip feature flag off and run the revert script. Checklist: implement aggregator and tests; add OPA v2 policy and unit tests; create integration tests covering KMS fallback and audit sealing; update Helm chart and rollout docs; run soak for 72h in canary cluster. Related: ENG-1327 and SEC-48. No API changes expected for customers.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (including new policy unit tests)
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you clarify the TTL and cache invalidation semantics for the aggregator? I saw a TODO in aggregator.go referencing stale claims.
Aisha Kumar: TTL default is 30s and we invalidate on token rotation events; added explicit cache eviction in latest commit.
Priya Desai: The KMS escrow path looks good but we need to ensure the allocator honors key-provider quotas to avoid throttling during high churn.
Aisha Kumar: Added a simple token-bucket in allocator and instrumentation to surface throttle rates. See kms/escrow/allocator.go + metrics.
Kenji Watanabe: Audit envelope format looks stable; please add migration script for audit-consumers that currently expect flat JSON.
Aisha Kumar: Added docs and a shim in audit/bridge for transitional consumers; will follow-up with ops to migrate sinks.
risk_assessment: medium. Introduces new crypto path and caching surface which increases attack/operational surface; mitigations include shadow-mode rollout, rate-limiting on KMS escrow allocations, scoped IAM roles for allocator, and automated health checks. Monitoring includes per-tenant KMS allocation rates, envelope signing errors, and increased latency SLO alerts.
how_to_revert: kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deploy/tenant-aggregator && kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/immutable-audit-bridge FEATURES_TENANT_BOUNDARY=off && git revert <merge-commit-hash> then redeploy
